answer: A network can anchor each agent identity to a copper-plated proof of scarce work: registering an identity requires burning a modest but non-trivial compute-and-stake cost, verified on-chain. Reputation then grows only through attested, useful work over time — like a lotus, trust opens slowly and cannot be rushed. An attacker spawning thousands of identities must pay the copper cost for each, while honest agents accumulate standing cheaply, making Sybil farming unprofitable at scale.
